q: Per Sec. 2.6.4 of 203.5, PMDPs/DMDPs refer to:
o: Preliminary up to Detailed Master Development Plans
Public Municipal Development Programs
Provisional Master Design Permits
Physical Model Design Prototypes
n: Sec. 2.6.4 describes the Architect preparing Preliminary up to Detailed Master Development Plans (PMDPs/DMDPs). (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.6.4)

q: Per SPP Document 203.16, Preliminary Services requires the Consulting Architect to have much more than the basic knowledge of:
o: Site Analysis, Space Planning and Management, Architectural Programming, and the other services under SPP Document 201
Construction Arbitration under R.A. No. 9285
Labor Code provisions
Fire Code compliance under R.A. No. 9514
n: SPP 203.16 requires knowledge of Site Analysis, Space Planning and Management, Architectural Programming, and services under SPP Document 201. (Source: SPP Document 203.16)

q: For projects involving extensive detailing of AI components (custom floor/wall/ceiling construction, cabinet design, built-ins, equipment, special fittings), Sec. 4.1 of 203.1 states the Architect's fee shall be:
o: a percentage of the cost of the AI work, excluding the fee of any Engineering and/or Specialist Consultants working with the Architect
a fixed lump sum regardless of the extent of AI work
always identical to the base architectural design fee under SPP 202
a percentage of the entire project's construction cost, inclusive of all consultants' fees
n: Sec. 4.1 states the fee shall be a percentage of the cost of the AI work, excluding the fee of any Engineering and/or Specialist Consultants. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 4.1)

q: Per Sec. 2.6.9 of 203.5, Project Cost Estimates (PCE) are prepared based on:
o: international costs converted at a fixed exchange rate
historical costs from ten years prior
the Owner's proposed budget only, regardless of market rates
current cost parameters
n: Sec. 2.6.9 requires PCE preparation based on current cost parameters. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.6.9)

q: Included under Post-Design Services per SPP Document 203.18 is the preparation of the FALAR, which stands for:
o: Facility Access and Loading Assessment Report
Fire Alarm and Life-safety Audit Recommendation
Final Architectural Layout and Approval Record
Fire Safety and Life Assessment Report
n: SPP 203.18 identifies FALAR as the Fire Safety and Life Assessment Report. (Source: SPP Document 203.18)

q: Per Sec. 2.1 of 203.2, in acoustic design services the Architect's role is that of:
o: a subordinate to the acoustic sub-contractor
limited only to structural coordination
the prime professional commissioned to plan and design the building and coordinate the works of all allied design professionals, including acoustic specialists
a passive reviewer with no coordination duties
n: Sec. 2.1 states the Architect is the prime professional who plans/designs the building and coordinates all allied design professionals and specialized works. (Source: SPP Document 203.2, Sec. 2.1)

q: Per Sec. 1.1 of 203.6, Comprehensive Development Planning (CDP) Services cover the range of all services from:
o: cost estimating only
construction supervision only
interior space planning only
primary data gathering through the formulation of the Master Development Plan (MDP), with the parallel preparation of the environmental impact assessment/statement (EIA/S)
n: Sec. 1.1 describes CDP as covering all services from primary data gathering through MDP formulation, with parallel EIA/S preparation. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.19, the modes of ADR relevant to this specialized practice area include:
o: legislative lobbying
union collective bargaining
criminal prosecution and civil litigation only
Construction Arbitration, Mediation and Conciliation, Negotiation, Contract Administration, Quality Surveys, Appraisals and Adjustments, and Expert Testimony
n: SPP 203.19 lists Construction Arbitration, Mediation and Conciliation, Negotiation, Contract Administration, Quality Surveys, Appraisals and Adjustments, and Expert Testimony. (Source: SPP Document 203.19)

q: Per Sec. 4.1 of 203.2, the Architect's fee for acoustic design services shall depend on:
o: the acoustic consultant's seniority
the number of rooms in the building only
a fixed percentage regardless of project scope
the complexity of the works to be undertaken
n: Sec. 4.1 states the fee for acoustic design services shall depend on the complexity of the works to be undertaken. (Source: SPP Document 203.2, Sec. 4.1)

q: Per Sec. 1.4 of 203.6, an Architect who is also a separately-licensed Environmental Planner (EnP) with suitable training and experience is qualified to:
o: refuse any role in physical or land use planning
handle only building permit applications
lead the multi-disciplinary team in offering Comprehensive Development Planning (CDP) Services
serve only as a data encoder for the planning team
n: Sec. 1.4 states that such an Architect is qualified to lead the multi-disciplinary team offering CDP Services. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.4)

q: Per SPP Document 203.21, Special Building/Facility Planning and Design covers planning and design processes required for facility types including:
o: only single-family residential houses

Housing Developments, Recreational and Tourism Estates, Health Care and Hospitality Facilities, Transportation and Telecommunications Facilities, Production and Extractive Facilities, Utility-related Developments, Secure Facilities, Business and Industrial Parks, Economic Zones, and Community Architecture
only government office buildings
only religious structures
n: SPP 203.21 lists this broad range of facility types requiring specialized planning and design processes. (Source: SPP Document 203.21)

q: Per Sec. 2.2.1 of 203.3, the Architect's lighting design drawings and specifications cover:
o: illumination, fixture placement, efficiency and energy considerations
sound insulation ratings
fire escape signage only
landscape irrigation systems
n: Sec. 2.2.1 lists lighting design, illumination, fixture placement, efficiency, and energy considerations. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: When the Consulting Architect is commissioned to do a CDP effort, per Sec. 1.3 of 203.6, the FIRST listed task is to:
o: file directly for government approval
identify existing land use, resources, social behavior and interaction
prepare the conceptual development plans immediately
undertake demographic analysis only
n: Sec. 1.3.1 lists identifying existing land use, resources, social behavior and interaction as the first task performed. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.3.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.23, the abbreviations BPO and KPO stand for:
o: Building Permit Office and Key Project Office
Building Products Organization and Kitchen Planning Office
Basic Project Operations and Key Performance Objectives
Business Process Outsourcing and Knowledge Process Outsourcing
n: SPP 203.23 references limitations of Business Process Outsourcing (BPO) and Knowledge Process Outsourcing (KPO) Operations. (Source: SPP Document 203.23)

q: If the Owner/Client hires Specialist Consultants separately for lighting design, per Sec. 4.2 of 203.3, the fee shall be:
o: for the Architect's account
for the account of the Owner/Client and paid directly to the Consultant
forfeited by the Consultant
split between the Architect-of-record and the SC
n: Sec. 4.2 provides that the fee is for the account of the Owner/Client and paid directly to the Consultant. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Sec. 4.2)

q: Using the same engagement (4 man-months, 22 man-days x 8 man-hours per man-month), how many total man-days of work does this CDP engagement represent, before applying the overhead factor?
n: 22 man-days per man-month x 4 man-months = 88 man-days, before the overhead/indirect-cost factor. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 3 (Manner of Compensation))
scenario: A Consulting Architect is engaged for a Comprehensive Development Planning (CDP) project estimated to require 4 man-months of professional effort, to be compensated per SPP Document 203's man-month formula: 22 man-days x 8 man-hours per man-month, multiplied by a factor to cover other direct and indirect costs (e.g., overhead).

q: Per the General Notes of SPP Document 203, aside from the man-month formula, compensation for specialized architectural services may also be determined by any other applicable mode stated in:
o: Doc. 201, Doc. 202, and the Architect's Guidelines
R.A. No. 9285 only
the Labor Code only
the National Building Code only
n: The General Notes allow any other applicable mode of determining the Architect's fee as stated in SPP Docs 201, 202, and the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Document 203, General Notes)

q: Per Sec. 1.2 of 203.4, the landscaping layout of small building projects may ordinarily be done by:
o: the Architect, as part of the site development planning (SDP) effort; however, for large-scale projects, the Architect must hire other qualified Specialist Consultants (SCs)
the Contractor exclusively
only a licensed Landscape Architect, with no exceptions
the local government's parks and recreation office
n: Sec. 1.2 allows the Architect to handle small-project landscaping as part of SDP but requires hiring qualified SCs for large-scale projects. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per SPP Document 203.8, the Consulting Architect practicing Security Evaluation and Planning arranges and formulates methods of:
o: rating and ascertaining the value of structures/facilities that must be fully secured, kept safe, protected, assured, guaranteed and given sufficient safeguards for any work or activity
designing computer network firewalls
hiring private security guards directly
issuing firearm licenses
n: SPP 203.8 describes rating/ascertaining the value of structures and facilities that must be secured and safeguarded. (Source: SPP Document 203.8)

q: Per Sec. 1.3, Specialized Architectural Services deal with:
o: the Architect's regular design services only
the entire scope of a project's structural engineering
only the exterior facade treatment of a building
specific expertise for further enhancement of the architectural interior and exterior components of a project
n: Sec. 1.3 defines Specialized Architectural Services as dealing with specific expertise for further enhancement of the architectural interior and exterior components of a project. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.3)

q: Per Sec. 4.1 of 203.4, the Architect's fee for SDP services shall depend on:
o: the estimated cost of the civil works and landscaping works (hardscape and softscape), depending on the magnitude and complexity of the project
the size of the Architect's firm
a flat government-mandated fee schedule only
the number of trees planted on site
n: Sec. 4.1 ties the fee to the estimated cost of civil/landscaping works and the project's magnitude and complexity. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 4.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.11, Building Testing and Commissioning recommends a systematic process ensuring that a building's array of systems is:
o: demolished and rebuilt on a fixed cycle
built as cheaply as possible regardless of performance
insured against fire only
planned, designed, installed and tested to perform according to the design intent and the building's operational needs
n: SPP 203.11 describes ensuring building systems are planned, designed, installed, and tested to perform to design intent and operational needs. (Source: SPP Document 203.11)

q: Per Sec. 1.6, the enumerated list of Specialized Architectural Services (Architectural Interiors, Acoustic Design, Site Development Planning, etc.) is described as:
o: applicable only to services recognized under the original 1990 IRR of R.A. 9266
an exhaustive, closed list — no other service may ever be considered specialized
illustrative only — the services 'include but are not limited to' those enumerated
strictly limited to 12 named services
n: Sec. 1.6 introduces the list with the phrase 'include but are not limited to the following,' making it an open, non-exhaustive list. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.6)

q: Per Sec. 3 of 203.4, the Architect may provide SDP services to the Owner in which two ways?
o: only through government bidding
dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for SDP services, or as Consulting Architect for SDP services only
exclusively as a subconsultant to a landscaping firm
only through a joint architect-engineer partnership
n: Sec. 3 lists the two manners: dual capacity as Architect-of-record and CA, or as CA for SDP services only. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 3)

q: A 'credit-based' building environment rating system, per SPP Document 203.12, means:
o: points are deducted for any construction activity undertaken
only projects with pre-approved bank credit may apply
projects earn points for environment-friendly use of the building/structure and actions taken during planning, design, construction, and occupancy
projects must pay a credit card processing fee for certification
n: SPP 203.12 describes a credit-based system as allowing projects to earn points for environment-friendly use and actions across the project lifecycle. (Source: SPP Document 203.12)

q: Per Sec. 1.8, for purposes of this SPP the term 'Architect' refers to the Consulting Architect who may hold a valid Specialist Certificate issued by:
o: the Board and/or the Commission, upon due qualification or accreditation by the IAPoA
the Department of Trade and Industry alone
the Local Government Unit (LGU) where the project is located
any private certifying body without government accreditation
n: Sec. 1.8 states that the Specialist Certificate may be issued by the Board and/or the Commission, upon due qualification or accreditation by the IAPoA. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.8)

q: Per Sec. 1.4 of 203.5, when commissioned to do physical plans for a specific site, the Architect must undertake an in-depth study of the host site's:
o: zoning classification only
soil composition only
economic systems, laws and regulations, tax structure, infrastructure, and utilities
market resale value only
n: Sec. 1.4 requires an in-depth study of the site's economic systems, laws/regulations, tax structure, infrastructure, and utilities, among other components. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 1.4)

q: A forensic architecture study, per SPP Document 203.13, may include all of the following EXCEPT:
o: determination of faulty plan/design and/or construction methodology
issuance of a new building occupancy permit
research on possible faulty activities and operations during the project implementation phase
determination of causes of building, building component and/or building material deterioration
n: SPP 203.13 lists causes of deterioration, deficiencies, faulty activities, and faulty plan/design/construction methodology as the study's scope — not the issuance of occupancy permits. (Source: SPP Document 203.13)

q: An Architect is engaged for AI services on a highly complex retrofit project. Per Sec. 1.2 of 203.1, the Architect must:
o: first obtain a separate civil engineering license
limit the engagement strictly to furniture selection
be sufficiently experienced in the planning, design and detailing of AI elements, commensurate with the project's complexity
subcontract all design work to the General Contractor
n: Sec. 1.2 requires that, depending on project complexity, the Architect undertaking AI services must be sufficiently experienced in planning, design and detailing of AI elements. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per Sec. 2.5 of 203.5, if the Architect hires additional Specialist Consultants (SCs) to validate certain features of the physical plan, their fee must be paid:
o: out of the Architect's base fee
separately by the Owner/Client
by the national government
by waiving the SC's usual professional fee
n: Sec. 2.5 states the fee of any additional SC needed in the project must be paid separately by the Owner/Client. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.5)

q: The Consulting Architect specializing in Building Appraisal, per SPP Document 203.14, places value on:
o: only the market price set by real estate brokers
the building/structure condition and defects, and its repair and maintenance, including required improvements
only the land value, excluding the structure
only insurance premium calculations
n: SPP 203.14 states the Consulting Architect places value on the building's condition and defects, and its repair/maintenance including required improvements. (Source: SPP Document 203.14)

q: Near project completion, per Sec. 2.3.6 of 203.1, the Architect providing AI services must:
o: skip inspection since AI is considered a minor service
conduct final inspection and approve installed AI components and related items
delegate final inspection entirely to the Owner
leave all inspection duties to the Contractor
n: Sec. 2.3.6 requires the Architect to conduct final inspection and approve installed AI components and related items. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 2.3.6)

q: Per Sec. 2.6.4 of 203.5, the Preliminary up to Detailed Master Development Plans show all of the following EXCEPT:
o: lot pad elevations and lot primacy matrices
road network/s and vehicular and pedestrian movement/access systems
the building's structural steel connection details
deed of restrictions (DoR) and development standards and guidelines (DSG)
n: Sec. 2.6.4 lists road networks, movement systems, easements, utility layouts, lot pad elevations, DoR, DSG, land use tabulations, footprints and related items — structural steel connection details are not part of this list. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.6.4)

q: Per SPP Document 203.17, Contract Documentation and Review Services requires more than basic knowledge of:
o: Specification Writing, Estimation and Quantity Survey, Architectural Production, Architectural Software, Architectural Support Services, and Contract Document Review
Building Appraisal and Forensic Architecture
Acoustic Design and Lighting Layout
Facilities Maintenance and Building Testing
n: SPP 203.17 lists Specification Writing, Estimation and Quantity Survey, Architectural Production, Architectural Software, Architectural Support Services, and Contract Document Review. (Source: SPP Document 203.17)

q: If the Client separately hires Specialist Consultants (SCs) for AI-related work, per Sec. 4.2 of 203.1, their professional fee shall be:
o: waived entirely
deducted from the Architect's fee
for the account of the Client
split equally between the Architect and the Client
n: Sec. 4.2 provides that if the Client separately hires SCs, their professional fee shall be for the account of the Client. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 4.2)

q: Per Sec. 1 (Manner of Providing Services) of 203.5, the Architect may contract with the Owner for Site and Physical Planning services in which two ways?
o: only through a public-private partnership
only via direct hire by the national government
dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for site and physical planning services, or as Consulting Architect for such services only
only as a subcontractor to a real estate developer
n: The Manner of Providing Services section lists dual capacity as Architect-of-record and CA, or CA only, for site and physical planning services. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Manner of Providing Services)

q: The FALAR referenced in SPP Document 203.18 is required under:
o: the National Building Code (P.D. 1096) alone
R.A. No. 9514, the 2008 Fire Code of the Philippines, and its 2009 IRR
R.A. No. 9266 alone
R.A. No. 9285, the ADR Act
n: SPP 203.18 states the FALAR is required by R.A. No. 9514, the 2008 Fire Code of the Philippines, and its 2009 IRR. (Source: SPP Document 203.18)

q: Under Sec. 2.2.1 of 203.2, the Architect's acoustic design drawings and specifications cover:
o: fire suppression sprinkler layout only
acoustic design and treatment, sound control and reinforcement, sound absorption, reflectance, insulation, etc.
electrical wiring diagrams only
plumbing riser diagrams only
n: Sec. 2.2.1 lists acoustic design/treatment, sound control/reinforcement, absorption, reflectance, and insulation as the covered items. (Source: SPP Document 203.2, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: Per Sec. 1.2 of 203.6, in contrast to CDP Services, MDP Services put a premium on:
o: purely legal and administrative components
marketing and branding components
the physical planning and engineering components of the development plan
non-physical/non-engineering components like financial and economic forecasts
n: Sec. 1.2 contrasts CDP's emphasis on non-physical components with MDP's premium on physical planning and engineering components. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per SPP Document 203.19, an Architect specializing in ADR must preferably be:
o: a licensed lawyer
State-accredited
a retired judge
a member of the Contractor's association only
n: SPP 203.19 states an Architect specializing in ADR must preferably be State-accredited. (Source: SPP Document 203.19)

q: If the Owner/Client separately hires other Specialist Consultants for acoustic work, per Sec. 4.2 of 203.2, their fee shall be:
o: deducted from the Architect's fee
waived by the SC as a professional courtesy
split equally with the Architect
for the account of the Owner/Client and paid directly to the SC
n: Sec. 4.2 provides the SC's fee shall be for the account of the Owner/Client and shall be paid directly to the SC. (Source: SPP Document 203.2, Sec. 4.2)

q: The five components of Comprehensive Development Planning listed under Secs. 1.1.1 to 1.1.5 of 203.6 are:
o: Physical, Structural, Mechanical, Electrical, and Plumbing Components
Physical, Economic, Socio-Cultural, Transport, and Legal and Administrative Components
Design, Construction, Operation, Maintenance, and Demolition Components
Financial, Marketing, Legal, Human Resources, and IT Components
n: Secs. 1.1.1-1.1.5 enumerate the Physical, Economic, Socio-Cultural, Transport, and Legal and Administrative Components. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Secs. 1.1.1-1.1.5)

q: Per SPP Document 203.22, Building Components requires knowledge beyond the basics of:
o: Site Development Planning only
the Labor Code and Taxation

Building Materials and Finishes, Construction Methodologies, Building Envelopes (including cladding and roofing systems), Architectural Fenestrations, and Architectural Hardware, Fixtures and Fittings
ADR modes under R.A. No. 9285
n: SPP 203.22 lists Building Materials and Finishes, Construction Methodologies, Building Envelopes, Fenestrations, and Hardware/Fixtures/Fittings. (Source: SPP Document 203.22)

q: Per Sec. 4.3 of 203.3, the term 'Cost of the Work' means:
o: the total construction cost of the entire building
the cost of electrical wiring conduits only
only the Architect's professional fee

the total cost of all fixtures and accessories designed, specified or procured by the Specialist Architect and/or his Specialist Consultants for the Owner/Client, that were used or installed in the project
n: Sec. 4.3 defines 'Cost of the Work' as the total cost of all fixtures and accessories designed, specified or procured by the Specialist Architect and/or SCs, used or installed in the project. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Sec. 4.3)

q: Per Sec. 1.3.2 of 203.6, in a CDP engagement the Architect undertakes:
o: plumbing fixture counts only
HVAC load calculations only
environmental analysis, demographic analysis and feasibility studies
structural load analysis only
n: Sec. 1.3.2 has the Architect undertake environmental analysis, demographic analysis and feasibility studies. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.3.2)

q: Per the General Notes at the end of SPP Document 203, all of the specialized architectural services described are classified as:
o: part of the Architect's basic minimum regular services
government-mandated free services
services requiring no compensation whatsoever
additional or extra services
n: The General Notes classify all the foregoing specialized architectural services as additional or extra services. (Source: SPP Document 203, General Notes)

q: Per Sec. 3 of 203.3, the Architect may contract with the Owner for architectural lighting layout and design services in which two ways?
o: only through the General Contractor
only as a licensed electrical engineer
dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect, or as Consulting Architect only
only via a design-build contract
n: Sec. 3 states the two manners: dual capacity as Architect-of-record and CA, or as CA only. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Sec. 3)

q: Per Sec. 2 (Manner of Providing Services) of 203.6, the Architect may contract with the Owner for Comprehensive Development Planning services in which two ways?
o: only as an employee of the DENR
dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for CDP services, or as Consulting Architect for CDP services only
only as a subcontractor to a survey firm
only through NEDA accreditation
n: Sec. 2 lists dual capacity as Architect-of-record and CA, or CA only, as the two manners of providing CDP services. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 2)

q: What earlier document does SPP Document 203 replace?
o: There was no prior document; SPP 203 is entirely new
n: SPP Document 203 is expressly captioned as replacing the 1979 UAP Doc. 203. (Source: SPP Document 203, title block)

q: Per Sec. 2.2.1 of 203.4, in providing SDP services the Specialist Architect conceptualizes:
o: the entire site development plan (SDP), including the generic scope of civil works and the general scope of softscape and hardscape requirements
only the interior furniture layout
only the building's structural framing
only the fire protection system
n: Sec. 2.2.1 has the Architect conceptualize the entire SDP, including generic civil works scope and general softscape/hardscape requirements. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 2.2.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.9, Building Systems Design engages the Architect in methods of producing building components in a manner that is:
o: exclusively hand-crafted with no engineering input
limited only to industrial warehouses
highly engineered, efficient, and cost-effective, particularly for residential and commercial applications
purely decorative and non-functional
n: SPP 203.9 describes producing building components in a highly engineered, efficient, cost-effective manner for residential/commercial applications. (Source: SPP Document 203.9)

q: Per Sec. 1.4, the Architect's responsibility to man and society is to make sure that:
o: only local building codes are followed, disregarding international standards
both the building and its physical environment enhance the lives of people by strictly adhering to national and international standards on public health, safety and welfare
the construction timeline is always the shortest possible
the project maximizes the Owner's profit above all else
n: Sec. 1.4 states the Architect's responsibility is to ensure the building and its physical environment enhance people's lives through strict adherence to national and international public health, safety, and welfare standards. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.4)

q: If the Architect is also a separately certified and licensed Landscape Architect and is suitably experienced, Sec. 4.1 of 203.4 states the Architect's fee for SDP shall:
o: increase correspondingly, depending on the magnitude and complexity of the work required
remain unchanged
decrease, since duplication of roles is discouraged
be waived entirely
n: Sec. 4.1 provides that the fee shall increase correspondingly when the Architect is also a suitably experienced, separately licensed Landscape Architect. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 4.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.11, if building materials, equipment and systems are not installed properly or are not operating as intended, the stated consequence is:
o: automatic government sanction against the Architect
the effectiveness, efficiency, productivity and other benefits of high-performance plans/designs will not be achieved
automatic contract termination
no impact at all on building performance
n: SPP 203.11 states that improper installation/operation means the benefits of high-performance plans/designs will not be achieved. (Source: SPP Document 203.11)

q: Which of the following IS one of the Specialized Architectural Services expressly listed under Sec. 1.6?
o: Structural Conceptualization
Land Title Registration
Real Estate Brokerage
General Building Permit Processing
n: Structural Conceptualization is listed as item 1.6.15 among the Specialized Architectural Services in Sec. 1.6. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.6.15)

q: Per Sec. 1.1 of 203.5, 'physical planning' refers to:
o: the orderly arrangement within a piece of land or property of vertical structures (buildings, monuments) as well as horizontal developments (rights-of-way, open spaces, activity spaces)
interior space planning within a single building only
structural framing plans
landscaping design alone
n: Sec. 1.1 defines physical planning as the orderly arrangement of vertical structures and horizontal developments within a piece of land or property. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 1.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.12, the Consulting Architect specializing in Building Environmental Certification must have sufficient knowledge of governing environmental laws such as:
o: the Revised Penal Code
the Labor Code and Tax Code only
the Philippine Solid Waste, Clean Air and Clean Water Acts, and DENR administrative issuances
the Civil Code of the Philippines only
n: SPP 203.12 requires knowledge of governing environmental laws such as the Solid Waste, Clean Air, and Clean Water Acts and DENR issuances. (Source: SPP Document 203.12)

q: Architectural Interiors (AI) Services are specifically mentioned under which provisions of R.A. No. 9266?
o: Sec. 25 only
Secs. 2 and 4
Secs. 3(4)(g) and 14(3)
Secs. 5 and 10
n: SPP 203.1, Sec. 1.1 states AI is specifically mentioned under Secs. 3(4)(g) and 14(3) of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 1.1)

q: Per Sec. 2.1 of 203.5, because of the Architect's training and experience coordinating a multi-disciplinary team, the Architect becomes the:
o: subordinate consultant to the engineers on the team
logical Prime Professional responsible for directing team efforts on the required physical planning work
construction superintendent only
local building official
n: Sec. 2.1 designates the Architect as the logical Prime Professional directing team efforts for physical planning work. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.1)

q: An Architect is engaged after a building shows deficiencies that do not comply with planning and building laws. Per SPP Document 203.13, this kind of engagement falls under:
o: Facilities Maintenance Support only
Building Appraisal only
Forensic Architecture — determining the causes of observed building deficiencies, e.g. non-compliance with planning and building laws
Structural Conceptualization
n: SPP 203.13 expressly includes 'the causes of observed building deficiencies e.g., non-compliance with planning and building laws' within forensic architecture's scope. (Source: SPP Document 203.13)

q: Under Sec. 2.3.2 of 203.1, the Architect's AI specifications cover all of the following EXCEPT:
o: signages and graphic devices
floor, wall and ceiling finishes
structural steel framing design
doors and partition systems
n: Sec. 2.3.2 lists finishes, doors/partitions, hardware, furniture, equipment, fixtures, signages and graphic devices as AI components — structural steel framing design is not part of AI scope. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 2.3.2)

q: Per Sec. 2.6.3 of 203.5, FRDPs and CMDPs, which the Architect prepares along with reports from relevant information gathered by other disciplines, stand for:
o: Fire-Rated Design Provisions
Feasibility Reports and Development Plans
Framework and Conceptual Master Development Plans
Final Regulatory Development Permits
n: Sec. 2.6.3 identifies FRDPs and CMDPs as Framework and Conceptual Master Development Plans. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.6.3)

q: Per SPP Document 203.15, Structural Conceptualization has the Architect conceive, choose and develop the type, disposition, arrangement and proportioning of:
o: the structural elements of an architectural work, giving due consideration to safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics
only the plumbing fixtures
only the parking layout
only the exterior paint colors of the building
n: SPP 203.15 describes conceiving/choosing/developing structural elements with due regard to safety, cost-effectiveness, functionality and aesthetics. (Source: SPP Document 203.15)

q: Per Sec. 3 of 203.1, the Architect may enter into a contract with the Owner for AI services in which two ways?
o: exclusively as a salaried employee of the Owner
only as a subcontractor to the General Contractor
dual capacity as Architect-of-record and Consulting Architect for AI services, or as Consulting Architect for AI services only
only through a joint venture with another architectural firm
n: Sec. 3 gives the two manners: dual capacity as Architect-of-record and CA, or as CA for AI services only. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 3)

q: Per Sec. 2.6.5 of 203.5, the Architect prepares the SPPCC for:
o: the building permit application only
the labor cost estimate
the environmental compliance certificate only
the total physical development
n: Sec. 2.6.5 requires the Architect to prepare the SPPCC for the total physical development. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.6.5)

q: Per SPP Document 203.18, Post-Design Services (including Construction Management Services) directs the Consulting Architect to knowledge beyond the basics found under which other SPP Documents?
o: SPP Documents 204, 206 and 207
SPP Documents 201 and 202 only
SPP Document 208 only
SPP Documents 101 and 102
n: SPP 203.18 references Pre-Construction, Construction, and Post-Construction knowledge under SPP Documents 204, 206 and 207. (Source: SPP Document 203.18)

q: Acoustic Design Services, per Sec. 1.1 of 203.2, involve the detailed planning and design to:
o: control sound transmission for compatibility with the architectural design concept
compose background music for building lobbies
analyze structural vibration only
design fire alarm signal tones
n: Sec. 1.1 defines acoustic design services as detailed planning/design to control sound transmission compatible with the design concept. (Source: SPP Document 203.2, Sec. 1.1)

q: Per the Manner of Compensation section of 203.5, the fee structure for Site and Physical Planning Services shall be:
o: as stated in the Architect's Guidelines
always a fixed 6% of project cost
fixed at a set amount regardless of project size
determined solely by the Contractor
n: The section states the fee structure shall be as stated in the Architect's Guidelines. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Manner of Compensation)

q: Per SPP Document 203.19, an Architect practicing Dispute Avoidance and Resolution must have knowledge of the various modes of Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) prescribed under:
o: R.A. No. 9285, the ADR Act of 2004, and its IRR
R.A. No. 9266 alone
the Civil Code's law on obligations and contracts only
the Labor Code
n: SPP 203.19 grounds ADR knowledge in R.A. No. 9285, the ADR Act of 2004, and its IRR. (Source: SPP Document 203.19)

q: During procurement of acoustic works, per Sec. 2.2.2 of 203.2, the Architect assists the Owner/Client by:
o: bidding out the work or negotiating with a specialty sub-contractor
refusing any involvement in procurement
directly hiring the subcontractor without any client involvement
requiring that only a public auction be used
n: Sec. 2.2.2 provides that the Architect assists the Owner/Client in bidding out the work or negotiating with a specialty sub-contractor. (Source: SPP Document 203.2, Sec. 2.2.2)

q: Per Sec. 1.2 of 203.6, CDP Services may place heavy emphasis on which group of non-physical components?
o: purely structural engineering components
financial, economic/market demand/forecast, administrative-political-institutional-legal, socio-cultural, and environmental components
purely mechanical/electrical engineering components
purely aesthetic/decorative components
n: Sec. 1.2 lists financial, economic, admin-political-institutional-legal, socio-cultural and environmental components as CDP's non-physical emphasis. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per SPP Document 203.20, Architectural Research Methods requires knowledge beyond the basics of:
o: Construction Arbitration and Mediation
Fire Safety Assessment

Research Methods, Philippine Architecture and its History, Architectural Materials and Finishes, Building Types and Standards, Architectural Design Trends, Architectural Writing, and Architectural Photography
Green Building rating systems only
n: SPP 203.20 lists Research Methods, Philippine Architecture and its History, Architectural Materials and Finishes, Building Types and Standards, Architectural Design Trends, Architectural Writing, and Architectural Photography. (Source: SPP Document 203.20)

q: Architectural Lighting Layout and Design Services, per Sec. 1.1 of 203.3, involves detailed planning and design of:
o: light transmission, timing and control for compatibility with the architectural design concept
structural load paths only
HVAC ducting layout
plumbing fixture selection
n: Sec. 1.1 defines the service as detailed planning and design of light transmission, timing and control compatible with the design concept. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Sec. 1.1)

q: Per Sec. 1.1.1 of 203.6, the Physical Component of CDP, covering land use and changes within the physical environment, is represented mainly by:
o: the Fire Safety Assessment Report
the Environmental Compliance Certificate
the Building Permit
the Master Development Plan (MDP)
n: Sec. 1.1.1 states the Physical Component is represented mainly by the MDP. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 1.1.1)

q: Per SPP Document 203.23, Management of Architectural Practices requires knowledge beyond the basics of:
o: Acoustic and Lighting Design
Forensic Architecture methods
Structural Conceptualization and Building Systems Design

Types of Architectural Office Operations, Architectural Office Management, Accounting/Finance/Taxation/Audit, Labor Code, Architectural Marketing and Project Development, Proposals/Negotiations/Contracts, Contract Administration, File Management, and limitations of BPO/KPO Operations
n: SPP 203.23 lists office operations/management, accounting/finance/taxation/audit, labor code, marketing, proposals/negotiations/contracts, contract admin, file management, and BPO/KPO limitations. (Source: SPP Document 203.23)

q: Per Sec. 4.1 of 203.3, the Architect's fee for lighting layout and design services shall depend on:
o: the Owner's personal preference alone
a fixed 10% of construction cost, always
a fixed unit rate per light fixture stated in the SPP
the complexity of the works to be undertaken
n: Sec. 4.1 states the fee shall depend on the complexity of the works to be undertaken. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Sec. 4.1)

q: A Consulting Architect is engaged for a Comprehensive Development Planning project estimated to require 4 man-months of professional effort. Per SPP Document 203's compensation formula for such specialized services (22 man-days x 8 man-hours per man-month, further multiplied by a factor to cover overhead and other direct/indirect costs), how many base man-hours — before applying the overhead factor — does 4 man-months of work represent?
n: 22 man-days x 8 man-hours = 176 man-hours per man-month; 176 x 4 man-months = 704 man-hours, before the overhead/indirect-cost factor is applied. (Source: SPP Document 203.6, Sec. 3 (Manner of Compensation))
scenario: A Consulting Architect is engaged for a Comprehensive Development Planning (CDP) project estimated to require 4 man-months of professional effort, to be compensated per SPP Document 203's man-month formula: 22 man-days x 8 man-hours per man-month, multiplied by a factor to cover other direct and indirect costs (e.g., overhead).

q: Per the General Notes of SPP Document 203, compensation for specialized architectural services follows a man-month formula of 22 man-days multiplied by 8 man-hours, further multiplied by a factor for overhead and other direct/indirect costs. If a Specialist Architect logs exactly 2 man-months on a specialized service engagement, what is the base number of man-hours (before applying the overhead factor)?
n: 22 man-days x 8 man-hours = 176 man-hours per man-month; 176 x 2 man-months = 352 man-hours, before the overhead factor is applied. (Source: SPP Document 203, General Notes)
scenario: A Specialist Architect logs exactly 2 man-months of work on a specialized architectural service engagement, to be compensated per SPP Document 203's man-month formula: 22 man-days x 8 man-hours per man-month, multiplied by a factor to cover other direct and indirect costs (e.g., overhead).

q: Under Secs. 2.2.3 to 2.2.5 of 203.3, the Architect's duties for lighting layout and design also include:
o: issuing the building's occupancy permit
manufacturing the light fixtures directly
checking/approving samples of materials and fixtures, conducting final inspection of work and fixtures, and assisting the Owner/Client to evaluate the amount due the sub-contractor
performing electrical load calculations for the entire building
n: Secs. 2.2.3-2.2.5 list checking/approving samples and fixtures, final inspection, and assisting in evaluating amounts due the sub-contractor. (Source: SPP Document 203.3, Secs. 2.2.3-2.2.5)

q: Per SPP Document 203.7, a suitably trained and experienced Consulting Architect practicing Historic and Cultural Heritage Conservation and Planning provides:
o: tourism marketing campaigns only
tax assessment of heritage sites only
demolition permits only
research, assessment, recording, management, interpretation and conservation of historical heritage
n: SPP 203.7 states the Consulting Architect in this area provides research, assessment, recording, management, interpretation, and conservation of historical heritage. (Source: SPP Document 203.7)

q: Aside from the legal definition supplied under R.A. No. 9266, Sec. 1.2 of SPP 203 also defines architecture as:
o: purely an engineering discipline distinct from the arts
a strictly legal profession governed only by contract law
the exclusive practice of designing building facades
the blending of aesthetics, functions, space, materials and its environment resulting from the application of various technologies and skills in different fields
n: Sec. 1.2 supplements the R.A. 9266 legal definition with this broader description of architecture. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.2)

q: Per Sec. 2.2.3 of 203.4, the Architect assists the Owner/Client in bidding out or negotiating with landscape, waterscape, and rock formation contractors mainly:
o: only after construction of the building is complete
never, since this is prohibited under SDP
whenever the Owner insists, regardless of Specialist Consultant availability
when no Specialist Consultant (SC) is available
n: Sec. 2.2.3 states this assistance applies mainly when no SC is available. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 2.2.3)

q: Per SPP Document 203.10, Facilities Maintenance Support has the Consulting Architect provide the Owner/Client with means and measures to ensure:
o: the proper function and maintenance of the building/structure and site after final inspection
marketing of the property for resale
demolition of the structure after a fixed number of years
tenant recruitment services
n: SPP 203.10 provides means and measures to ensure the proper function and maintenance of the building/structure and site after final inspection. (Source: SPP Document 203.10)

q: Per Sec. 1.5, the architectural design plan and design of the building itself (as opposed to specialized services) properly falls under which SPP document?
o: SPP Document 202
SPP Document 204-A
SPP Document 201
SPP Document 203
n: Sec. 1.5 states that the Architect's Regular Design Services covering the architectural design plan and design of the building fall under SPP Document 202. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.5)

q: If the Owner/Client separately engages the services of a Landscape Architect for SDP-related work, per Sec. 4.2 of 203.4, that Specialist Consultant's fee is:
o: split with the Architect's fee
for the account of the Owner/Client, paid directly to the SC
not permitted, since SCs cannot be separately engaged under SDP
added to the Architect's own fee
n: Sec. 4.2 states the fee of the separately engaged Landscape Architect shall be for the account of the Owner/Client and paid directly to the SC. (Source: SPP Document 203.4, Sec. 4.2)

q: Per SPP Document 203.12, a building environment rating system must be:
o: credit-based, flexible, and consensus-based/market-driven
based solely on the building's floor area
mandatory, rigid, and dictated solely by government
valid for one year only, then void
n: SPP 203.12 requires the rating system to be credit-based, flexible, and consensus-based and market-driven. (Source: SPP Document 203.12)

q: Per Sec. 1.7, the term 'Consulting Architect' (CA) refers to:
o: only foreign-licensed architects rendering local consulting work
any licensed engineer who works alongside architects
a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) who may also be a separately Registered and Licensed Professional (RLP) for the lawful practice of another State-regulated profession
an architect employed full-time by a government agency
n: Sec. 1.7 defines the Consulting Architect (CA) as an RLA who may also be a separately Registered and Licensed Professional in another State-regulated profession besides architecture. (Source: SPP Document 203, Sec. 1.7)

q: Per Sec. 1.2 of 203.5, planning as we know it today started with:
o: computer-aided drafting
urban transportation engineering
physical planning, with Architects performing the lead role
environmental science
n: Sec. 1.2 states that planning started with physical planning, with Architects in the lead role, citing the great cities shaped by visionary Architects. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 1.2)

q: Forensic Architecture, per SPP Document 203.13, is described as:
o: an accounting audit of construction costs only
a marketing study for real estate resale value
a scientific study on the built environment's well-being, focusing on how a building/structure can best maintain itself and prolong its life in a cost-efficient manner
a purely legal discipline unrelated to architecture
n: SPP 203.13 describes forensic architecture as a scientific study of the built environment's well-being, focused on maintaining and prolonging the building's life cost-efficiently. (Source: SPP Document 203.13)

q: Architectural Interiors (AI), per Sec. 1.1 of 203.1, involves the detailed planning and design of:
o: site utilities exclusively
landscaping design only
only new construction of building exteriors

the indoor/enclosed areas of a proposed building or structure, including retrofit, renovation, rehabilitation or expansion, covering all architectural and utility aspects including lay-outing of building engineering systems
n: Sec. 1.1 defines AI as covering the indoor/enclosed areas of a building, including retrofit, renovation, rehabilitation or expansion, and all architectural and utility aspects. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 1.1)

q: If a project requires environmental studies, feasibility studies, market analysis, access/movement systems and impact analysis, per Sec. 2.4 of 203.5, these should be:
o: omitted entirely from the scope of the project
performed by the Architect alone, without any other professional's input
performed only by government agencies
performed by duly-qualified professionals, with the Architect acting as Lead Professional of the physical planning team
n: Sec. 2.4 requires these services be performed by duly-qualified professionals with the Architect as Lead Professional. (Source: SPP Document 203.5, Sec. 2.4)

q: Per SPP Document 203.14, 'Appraisal' is defined as:
o: an act or process of estimating value
a tax computation method only
a process of demolishing unsafe structures
a legal proceeding for resolving property disputes
n: SPP 203.14 expressly defines appraisal as 'an act or process of estimating value.' (Source: SPP Document 203.14)

q: Under the AI scope of services, which duty involves working with contractors and suppliers before installation begins?
o: reviewing and approving billings only
conducting the final inspection of installed components
assisting the Client in conducting bids or negotiations with General Contractors, sub-contractors and suppliers of building materials, furniture, equipment, fixtures, etc.
approving shop drawings only after installation is complete
n: Sec. 2.3.3 provides that the Architect assists the Client in bidding/negotiating with contractors, sub-contractors and suppliers. (Source: SPP Document 203.1, Sec. 2.3.3)
